items.question: Is bondage attributed to all beings or only to the individual self?
premises: Māyā causes misidentification of the non-self as self.
The individual self, not all beings universally, is the locus of this bondage.
items.inference: Therefore bondage is held to belong to the individual self alone and not to all.
uncertainties: The referent of tayoḥ (of those two) is not explicitly identified within this verse.
items.plain_english: Therefore bondage is held, in the view of those two, to belong to the individual self alone, and not to all.
